readings.title: The Cedar Seed in the City of Merchants
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH illustrates the initial transfer of authority to a foreign power.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 17:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] “Son of man, put forth <dn>את</dn> a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Yisra’ĕl. [3] “And you shall say, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“The great eagle with large wings of long pinions, covered with feathers of various colours, came to Leḇanon and took <dn>את</dn> the top of the cedar.</dq> [4] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> plucked off <dn>את</dn> the topmost of its young twigs and brought it to a land of traders. In a city of merchants <dn>he</dn> placed it.</dq> [5] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> also took some of the seed of the land and planted it in a field for seed. <dn>He</dn> took it by many waters, set it like a willow tree.</dq> [6] <dq>“So it grew and became a low, spreading vine. Its branches turned toward him, and its roots were under it. And it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and sent out shoots.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Breach of the First Eagle
readings.title: The Vine Reaches for Another
readings.subtitle: The inevitable consequences of seeking strength outside the established decree.
readings.text: [7] <dq>“And there was another great eagle with large wings and many feathers. And see, this vine bent its roots toward him, and stretched its branches toward him, to water it, away from the beds where it was planted.</dq> [8] <dq>“It was planted in a good field by many waters, to bring forth branches, and to bear fruit, to be a splendid vine.”</dq> ’ [9] “Say, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Is it going to thrive? Is <dn>he</dn> not going to pull up its roots, and cut off its fruit, and let it wither? All of its sprouting leaves wither, without great power or many people, to pluck it up by its roots.</dq> [10] <dq>“See, it is planted, is it going to thrive? Would it not utterly wither when the east wind touches it – wither in the beds where it grows?”</dq> ’ ”

readings.title: The Vain Alliance with Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: Judah attempts to subvert Babylon's authority, breaking a sworn covenant.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 17:11] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [12] “Please say to the rebellious house, ‘Do you not know what these mean?’ Say, ‘See, the sovereign of Baḇel went to Yerushalayim and took its sovereign and heads, and brought them with <dn>את</dn> him to Baḇel. [13] And <dn>he</dn> took one of the royal seed, and made a covenant with <dn>את</dn> him, and put him under oath. And <dn>he</dn> took away <dn>את</dn> the mighty of the land, [14] so that the reign would be brought low and not lift itself up, but guard <dn>את</dn> his covenant, that it might stand. [15] But <dn>he</dn> rebelled against him by sending his messengers to Mitsrayim, to give him horses and many people. Shall <dn>he</dn> thrive? Shall <dn>he</dn> escape who is doing these? And shall <dn>he</dn> break a covenant and still escape?

readings.subsection: The Verdict of the Righteous Judge
readings.title: The Snare for the Oath-Breaker
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH executes justice against the one who despised His Name.
readings.text: [16] <dq>As <dn>I</dn> live,’</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘in the place where the sovereign dwells who set him up to reign, whose oath <dn>he</dn> despised and whose covenant <dn>he</dn> broke, with <dn>את</dn> him in the midst of Baḇel <dn>he</dn> shall die!</dq> [17] <dq>And Pharaoh with his great army and great company is not going to help him in battle, when they heap up a siege mound and build a wall to cut off many beings.</dq> [18] <dq>And <dn>he</dn> despised <dn>את</dn> the oath by breaking the covenant. And see, <dn>he</dn> has given his hand and <dn>he</dn> has done all this, <dn>he</dn> is not going to escape.’</dq> ” [19] Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“As <dn>I</dn> live, <dn>My</dn> oath which <dn>he</dn> has despised, and <dn>My</dn> covenant which <dn>he</dn> has broken, shall <dn>I</dn> not put it on his own head?</dq> [20] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall spread <dn>My</dn> net over him, and <dn>he</dn> shall be taken in <dn>My</dn> snare. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring him to Baḇel and enter into judgment with <dn>את</dn> him there for the trespass which <dn>he</dn> committed against <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [21] <dq>and all his fugitives with all his bands fall by the sword, and those who are left be scattered to every wind. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken.”</dq>

readings.title: The Tender Twig on the Lofty Mountain
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH promises to personally establish an enduring kingdom that reverses human hierarchies.
readings.text: [22] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall take of the top of the highest cedar and set it out. And <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall pluck off a tender one from the topmost of its young twigs, and plant it on a high and lofty mountain.</dq> [23] <dq>“On the mountain height of Yisra’ĕl <dn>I</dn> plant it. And it shall bring forth branches, and bear fruit, and become a big cedar. And under it shall dwell birds of every sort, in the shadow of its branches they shall dwell.</dq> [24] <dq>“And all the trees of the field shall know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have brought down the high tree and exalted the low tree, dried up the green tree and made the dry tree flourish. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken and shall do it.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Eradication of the Generational Proverb
readings.title: All Beings Are Mine
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH abolishes the myth of inherited guilt within the penal system.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 18:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] “What do you mean when you use this proverb concerning the land of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are blunted’? [3] <dq>“As <dn>I</dn> live,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“you shall no longer use this proverb in Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [4] <dq>“See, all beings are <dn>Mine</dn>, the being of the father as well as the being of the son is <dn>Mine</dn>. The being that is sinning shall die.</dq>

readings.title: Walking in Torah and Truth
readings.subtitle: The tangible actions that constitute a life perfectly aligned with YeHoVaH's order.
readings.text: [5] <dq>“But if a man is righteous and shall do right-ruling and righteousness,</dq> [6] <dq>if <dn>he</dn> has not eaten on the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Yisra’ĕl, nor defiled his neighbour’s wife, nor comes near a woman during her uncleanness,</dq> [7] <dq>if <dn>he</dn> does not oppress anyone, does return to the debtor his pledge, does not commit robbery, does give his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with a garment,</dq> [8] <dq>if <dn>he</dn> does not lend on interest or take increase, turns back his hand from unrighteousness, executes right-ruling in truth between man and man,</dq> [9] <dq>if <dn>he</dn> walks in <dn>My</dn> laws, and <dn>he</dn> has guarded <dn>My</dn> right-rulings in truth – <dn>he</dn> is righteous, <dn>he</dn> shall certainly live!”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Rebellious Son Bears His Own Blood
readings.subtitle: A righteous father does not exempt a son who embraces systemic disharmony.
readings.text: [10] <dq>“But if <dn>he</dn> has brought forth a son who is a robber or a shedder of blood, who does any of these –</dq> [11] <dq>whereas <dn>he</dn> himself did not do any of these – that also <dn>he</dn> has eaten on the mountains or defiled his neighbour’s wife,</dq> [12] <dq>if <dn>he</dn> has oppressed the poor and needy, has committed robbery, <dn>he</dn> does not return a pledge, has lifted his eyes to the idols, or did abomination,</dq> [13] <dq>if <dn>he</dn> has lent on interest or taken increase – shall <dn>he</dn> live? <dn>He</dn> shall not live! If <dn>he</dn> has done any of these abominations, <dn>he</dn> shall certainly die, his blood is upon him.</dq>

readings.title: The Son Who Chooses Life
readings.subtitle: Observing wickedness and actively choosing righteousness preserves the soul.
readings.text: [14] <dq>“But see, if <dn>he</dn> has brought forth a son who sees all the sins which his father has done, but <dn>he</dn> fears and does not do likewise,</dq> [15] <dq>has not eaten on the mountains, and has not lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Yisra’ĕl, has not defiled his neighbour’s wife,</dq> [16] <dq>has not oppressed anyone, nor withheld a pledge, nor committed robbery, has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with a garment,</dq> [17] <dq>turns back his hand from wronging the poor, and <dn>he</dn> has not taken interest or increase, has executed <dn>My</dn> right-rulings and walked in <dn>My</dn> laws – <dn>he</dn> shall not die for the crookedness of his father, <dn>he</dn> shall certainly live!</dq> [18] <dq>“<dn>His</dn> father, because <dn>he</dn> used oppression, robbed his brother, and did what is not good among his people, see, <dn>he</dn> shall die for his crookedness.</dq>

readings.title: The Weight of Righteousness and Rebellion
readings.subtitle: Past righteousness does not cover present unrighteousness.
readings.text: [19] <dq>“And you said, ‘Why should the son not bear the crookedness of the father?’ But the son has done right-ruling and righteousness, <dn>he</dn> has guarded all <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>he</dn> does them, <dn>he</dn> shall certainly live.</dq> [20] <dq>“The being who sins shall die. The son shall not bear the crookedness of the father, nor the father bear the crookedness of the son. The righteousness of the righteous is upon himself, and the wrongness of the wrong is upon himself.</dq> [21] <dq>“But the wrong, if <dn>he</dn> turns from all his sins which <dn>he</dn> has done, and <dn>he</dn> shall guard all <dn>My</dn> laws, and shall do right-ruling and righteousness, <dn>he</dn> shall certainly live, <dn>he</dn> shall not die.</dq> [22] <dq>“All the transgressions which <dn>he</dn> has done shall not be remembered against him – in his righteousness that <dn>he</dn> has done, <dn>he</dn> shall live.</dq> [23] <dq>“Have <dn>I</dn> any pleasure in the death of the wrong?”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Is it not that <dn>he</dn> should turn from his ways, and live?</dq> [24] <dq>“But when a righteous one turns away from his righteousness and does unrighteousness, according to all the abominations that the wrong one has done, shall <dn>he</dn> live? All his righteousness which <dn>he</dn> has done shall not be remembered. For his trespass which <dn>he</dn> has committed, and for his sin which <dn>he</dn> has committed, for them <dn>he</dn> shall die.</dq>

readings.title: Make for Yourselves a New Heart
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH pleads for sincere repentance, declaring His lack of pleasure in the death of the wicked.
readings.text: [25] <dq>“And you said, ‘The way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not right.’ Hear now, O house of Yisra’ĕl, is <dn>My</dn> way not right? Is it not your ways that are not right?</dq> [26] <dq>“When a righteous one turns away from his righteousness, and does unrighteousness, and <dn>he</dn> dies in it, it is because of his unrighteousness which <dn>he</dn> has done that <dn>he</dn> dies.</dq> [27] <dq>“And when the wrong turns away from the wrong which <dn>he</dn> has done, and <dn>he</dn> does right-ruling and righteousness, <dn>he</dn> keeps himself alive.</dq> [28] <dq>“Because <dn>he</dn> sees and turns away from all the transgressions which <dn>he</dn> has done, <dn>he</dn> shall certainly live, <dn>he</dn> shall not die.</dq> [29] <dq>“And the house of Yisra’ĕl have said, ‘The way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not right.’ Are <dn>My</dn> ways not right, O house of Yisra’ĕl? Is it not your ways that are not right?</dq> [30] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> judge you, O house of Yisra’ĕl, every one according to his ways,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Repent, and turn back from all your transgressions, and let not crookedness be a stumbling-block to you.</dq> [31] <dq>"Cast away from you all the transgressions, by which you have transgressed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Yisra’ĕl?</dq> [32] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have no pleasure in the death of one who dies,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“So turn back and live!”</dq>

readings.section: The Fall of the Royal House
readings.title: The Caged Lions of Yisra'el
readings.subtitle: The violent rise and inevitable capture of Judah's corrupted leadership.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 19:1] “And take up a lamentation for the leaders of Yisra’ĕl, [2] and you shall say, ‘What a lioness was your mother among the lions! She lay down among the lions, in the midst of the young lions she reared her cubs. [3] And she brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion. And he learned to tear the prey, he devoured men. [4] Then nations heard of him. He was caught in their pit, and they brought him with chains to the land of Mitsrayim. [5] When she saw, as she waited, that her expectancy was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion. [6] And he went about among the lions, and became a young lion. And he learned to tear the prey, he devoured men. [7] And he knew their widows, and laid waste their cities. And the land and all who filled it was stunned by the noise of his roaring. [8] Then nations set against him from the provinces on every side, and spread their net over him, he was caught in their pit. [9] And they put him in a cage in chains, and brought him to the sovereign of Baḇel. They brought him in nets, so his roar was no longer heard on the mountains of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.section: The Fall of the Royal House
readings.title: Planted in a Dry and Thirsty Land
readings.subtitle: The once-exalted kingdom is dried up by the east wind and consumed by fire.
readings.text: [10] Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the waters, a bearer of fruit and branching, because of many waters. [11] And she had strong rods for sceptres of rulers. And her stature was exalted among the thick branches, and was seen in her height with the mass of its branches. [12] But she was uprooted in wrath, she was cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried her fruit. Her strong rods were broken and withered, fire consumed them. [13] And now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land. [14] And fire went out from a rod of her branches. It devoured her fruit, so that she has no strong rod, a sceptre to rule.’ ” This is a lament, and it shall be a lament.
